The House met at eleven of the clock. 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
REFERENCE TO THE TERRORISTS ATTACK ON THE 
PARLIAMENT HOUSE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I rise to make reference to the 
cowardly and dastardly act of the terr orists, who attacked the Parliament 
Building yesterday, the 13 th December, 2001. It has shocked not only the 
entire Nation but also the conscience of freedom - loving humankind all over 
the world.   No words are strong  enough  to  condemn  this heinous act. 
As we are aware, seven persons, including four from my security, 
namely Shri Jagdish Prasad Yadav, Security Assistant, Watch and Ward, 
Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Shrimati Kamlesh Kumari of C.R.P.F., Shri 
Ghanshyam, Shri Nanak Chand, Shri  Ram Pal, Shri Om Prakash, all 
belonging to Delhi Police, Shri Desh Raj, Gardner belonging to CPWD were 
killed. Watch and Ward staff were unarmed, but showed great presence of 
mind. At least thirty persons, including  some security personnel were injured 
in the terrorists shoot-out and* some of them are in a critical condition. Our 
sympathies go to the victims of the attack and the bereaved families. 
Our security personnel and Watch an d Ward staff deserve praise for 
their alertness and devotion to their duty in highest traditions in intercepting 
and shooting down the terrorists. Their timely action averted a major 
catastrophe. 
I hope the whole House joins me in condemning this brutal and 
barbaric attack. We resolve to fight unitedly terrorism with grit and 
determination and shall eliminate it. This House extends its heartfelt 
condolences to the affected families in their hour of grief. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of those who laid down their precious lives in 
this tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 

 RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2001] 
MR.  CHAIRMAN :, The House stands adjourned till  11  a.m.  on 
Tuesday, the 18th December, 2001. 
The House then adjourned at three minutes past eleven of the clock till 
eleven of the clock on Tuesday, the 18th December, 2001.
